title: Hyring Insight Reports 10x Revenue Growth in 3 months
summary: Hyring’s newest workforce intelligence platform has grown 10x in revenue in just 90 days. Hyring , the emerging AI hiring platform , which to date has run 900,000 plus AI interviews, announced that its new product, Hyring Insight, has grown tenfold over the last 90 days. The company’s quick success comes from two key product decisions: transparency and Ask AI, an aide that helps explain what employees did during the workday. Hyring Insight is time tracking software that prides itself on transparent employee monitoring. It tracks their working hours, their activity, and the apps and websites they use, along with screenshots while the timer is running, and it uses artificial intelligence to explain where the workday went and what was achieved. AI-Generated Timesheet Insights A timesheet can tell managers if eight hours were worked. Hyring Insight predominantly uses AI to analyze the workday. Its Ask AI feature answers questions regarding time and activity. It holds back on making any final decisions about a person. There are four plans for clients to choose from. Free covers up to two users with 30 days of history included. They can then choose to upgrade to the Starter plan, the Pro plan, which gives automatic AI summaries, time-lapses, and alerts, or the Enterprise plan, which is built for enterprises with 50 or more users and adds remote vs office statistics, a read-only AI connector, SSO, SCIM, an audit log, API, and a custom DPA. If a client chooses annual billing, they save up to 30%. For paid plans, unusual activity is activity that differs from the employee’s own pattern, which may include any input that seems artificial. Each flag must be verified at the manager’s discretion, as Hyring Insight makes no recommendation. For employees, the app includes an avatar, streaks, music, and kudos from other colleagues. I think it’s disgusting. I think the people who run it are disgusting. They’ve made a massive gamble with humanity and society and culture.” His contempt may surprise anyone who’s familiar with Rankin’s substantial AI output. Ever since the artist Damien Hirst introduced him to the possibilities of generative AI in 2021, the British photographer has been going further down the rabbit hole. “I’m not somebody who likes to be critical about something without actually knowing about it,” he explains. “I’ve gone deep into trying to work it out.” Continue reading...
